搬.meaning: A tired <part>carrier</part> who rows goods across the harbour is sick of lifting crates. She ties her <part>anchor</part> rope round a loop of wooden rollers, and now every crate slides up from her boat to the warehouse on its own. She just sits and waves at them. She has invented the <kanji>conveyor</kanji>.
搬.on: The first crate up is full of jars of <sound>hon</sound>ey, and a bee rides along on top.

晶.meaning: A miner digs up a stone with three tiny <part>sun</part> shapes trapped inside. When she holds it to the window, each one throws rainbows round her hut, and her dog chases them for hours. Even at night it glows. She has never seen anything <kanji>sparkle</kanji> like that.
晶.on: She takes it on tour as the star of a travelling <sound>show</sound>.

秒.meaning: A chef drops a <part>few</part> kernels of <part>grain</part> into a sizzling pan and turns to fetch the salt. Pop, pop, pop! Before she turns back, every one has burst and flown out of the window. Popcorn waits for nobody: it's done in one <kanji>second</kanji>.
秒.on: Outside, a ba<sound>by</sound> bats each one away with his <sound>yo</sound>-yo.

俳.meaning: A cat poet finishes her supper and hangs the leftover <part>fishbone</part> on the <part>coat hook</part> by her door. Every night she stares at it and writes three short lines about it, never more. Her whole book is about one fish: a <kanji>haiku</kanji> for every bone.
俳.on: The bees in the <sound>hi</sound>ve next door hum each poem back to her.

胃.meaning: A greedy giant eats a whole <part>rice field</part> for lunch, paddies, frogs and all, then a slice of the <part>moon</part> for pudding. Lying in the grass, he hears croaking from inside and sees a silver glow through his shirt. All of it is sloshing in his <kanji>stomach</kanji>.
胃.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l he swallowed by mistake tickles him from the inside.

諸.meaning: At the village meeting, <part>someone</part> new climbs onto the barrel every minute to give a <part>speech</part>: the baker on bread, the goat on grass, a ghost on creaky doors, a toddler on jelly. Nobody agrees and nobody is bored. The topics are wildly <kanji>various</kanji>.
諸.on: Afterwards they all crowd into the corner <sound>sho</sound>p for snacks.
諸.kun: Last of all, a <sound>mo</sound>th gives a speech about a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket.

殊.meaning: A museum is full of grey dinosaur <part>bones</part>, all dusty and all alike. But one skeleton was dug out of <part>vermilion</part> clay and is bright red from skull to tail. Every school trip skips the others and runs straight to it. Children love that one <kanji>particularly</kanji>.
殊.on: The café sells little red <sound>su</sound>gar dinosaurs shaped just like it.
殊.kun: Even a <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>to</sound>rtoise queue up to see it.

愚.meaning: A boy feeds his whole piggy bank into a <part>gumball machine</part> because a sign says one ball hides a golden <part>heart</part>. Two hundred gumballs later his cheeks are bulging, his pockets are empty, and the heart turns out to be plastic. Grandad shakes his head: <kanji>foolish</kanji>.
愚.on: He carries the leftover gumballs home in a <sound>goo</sound>die bag to share.
愚.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' he sighs, and swaps the plastic heart for a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket.

刷.meaning: A pirate's cat steps in a pot of black ink, then strolls across every <part>towel</part> drying on deck, leaving pawprints everywhere. The captain loves the pattern. He hoists one towel as his new <part>flag</part> and cuts the rest into posters with his <part>dagger</part>. Paws are the fastest <kanji>printing</kanji> on the seas.
刷.on: He celebrates with a <sound>sats</sound>uma, peeling it with the dagger.
刷.kun: When the ink runs out, the cat walks through <sound>soo</sound>t from the stove instead.

廷.meaning: The queen's judge takes one <part>long stride</part> into the hall, sits down and spins wool on a <part>spindle</part> while both sides argue. When the thread is long enough, he snips it and gives his verdict. Nobody argues with the spinning judge of the royal <kanji>courts</kanji>.
廷.on: Each verdict is stuck to the hall door with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.

撲.meaning: A <part>porter</part> carries a tower of crates past a ship, and the sailor's <part>anchor</part>, swinging on its rope, keeps bumping the stack. So the porter, still balancing everything on his head, reaches out and gives the anchor one tidy <kanji>slap</kanji>. It stops swinging at once.
撲.on: A <sound>bo</sound>xer dog on deck barks his loud approval.

疫.meaning: In a <part>leaky shed</part> at the edge of the village, a <part>maiden</part> sneezes. By lunch the milkman is sneezing, by supper the whole village, and by Friday even the goats. The doctor pins up a map covered in red dots and sighs. It's an <kanji>epidemic</kanji>.
疫.on: Only a spiky <sound>echi</sound>dna stays well, curled in a ball with its nose tucked in.

飢.meaning: A snail sets a <part>table</part> for one and orders a feast. The waiter is also a snail. Hours pass, then days. Dust gathers on the tablecloth and the snail's tummy rumbles louder than thunder, but no <part>food</part> arrives. He has never been so <kanji>hungry</kanji>.
飢.on: At last the waiter crawls up with a <sound>key</sound> to the kitchen and a note saying sorry.
飢.kun: He orders a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and settles in to wait again.

碑.meaning: When the king's most <part>lowly</part> servant, the man who weeded the rice field, dies at a hundred, nobody expects a fuss. But the whole town carves him a <part>stone</part> taller than the palace, covered in tiny weeds and muddy boots. Visitors still polish his <kanji>tombstone</kanji>.
碑.on: Each visitor taps it with a boot <sound>hee</sound>l for luck.
碑.kun: Carved on it are an <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>shi</sound>eld, a <sound>boo</sound>k and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, his four favourite things.

逸.meaning: Half a mile into a marathon, the <part>rabbit</part> leading the runners spots a <part>ramp</part> down to a carrot farm and takes it. Two hundred runners follow him. The finish line waits all day. Nobody meant the race to <kanji>deviate</kanji> that far.
逸.on: Down on the farm, the rabbit <sound>eats</sound> carrots till sunset.
逸.kun: Then he naps on an old <sound>so</sound>fa in the middle of the field.

契.meaning: A <part>large</part> knight climbs onto the castle roof, raises his <part>sword</part> beside the <part>TV antenna</part> and swears, live on every screen in the kingdom, to guard the realm forever. Then he slips, and the antenna catches his belt. Dangling there, he repeats his <kanji>pledge</kanji>.
契.on: The queen sends up a slice of <sound>ca</sound>ke on a rope to keep him going.
契.kun: A <sound>chee</sound>tah and two <sound>gee</sound>se haul him back up by the boots.

祥.meaning: On the night the princess is born, a white <part>sheep</part> wanders into the square and curls up under the old <part>lamppost</part>, which flickers on by itself for the first time in years. The village elders nod at each other. Everyone agrees: it's <kanji>auspicious</kanji>.
祥.on: Every year on her birthday, the village puts on a puppet <sound>show</sound> about it.
祥.kun: The sheep gives a happy <sound>sigh</sound>, and the baby answers, '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

遮.meaning: A <part>commoner</part> sits at the foot of the palace <part>ramp</part> with a butterfly net. Every paper plane the princes throw from the balcony, he snatches mid-flight, refolds into a frog and hands back. Not one plane has landed in a year. He loves to <kanji>intercept</kanji>.
遮.on: One day he nets a stray <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock too.
遮.kun: He shares his lunch, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and an <sound>e</sound>gg, with two passing <sound>gee</sound>se.

癖.meaning: A spice seller runs her <part>chili stall</part> from a <part>leaky shed</part>. Every time a drip lands on her nose she tugs her left ear and winks, and now she does it with no drip at all, even in her sleep. Her customers wink back. It's her famous <kanji>mannerism</kanji>.
癖.on: She lays out her chilies in a neat <sound>hex</sound>agon on the counter.
癖.kun: Even her <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock seems to wink when it strikes <sound>se</sound>ven.

軌.meaning: Every morning a farmer drives his old <part>car</part> down the same lane to market, and after <part>nine</part> years its wheels have worn two deep grooves in the mud. Now he doesn't even steer. He reads the paper while the car follows the <kanji>rut</kanji>.
軌.on: He just turns the <sound>key</sound> and opens the sports page.

峰.meaning: A lazy climber gets halfway up a <part>mountain</part> and finds a <part>lookout post</part> with a folding chair on top. He climbs the post instead, sits down, and waves at the real climbers struggling above him. From his chair it feels just like the <kanji>summit</kanji>.
峰.on: Someone up top sprays him with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se for cheating.
峰.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat shares his chair and holds his butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t.

訂.meaning: A mayor writes a <part>speech</part> to open a new <part>street</part>. A dog chews page two, so he rewrites it; rain smudges page three, so he rewrites that; a pigeon lands on the rest. He scribbles all night under a lamp. By dawn it's version forty. He just loves to <kanji>revise</kanji>.
訂.on: He sticks each new page over the old one with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
訂.kun: At the opening he cries, '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!', and reads out a single word.

凸.meaning: A girl on the beach packs her <part>bucket</part> with wet sand and turns out a wide mound, then plonks a small wooden <part>frame</part> on top as a tower. A crab climbs to the peak and looks down at the bulge. Anything that swells outward like that, her teacher says, is <kanji>convex</kanji>.
凸.on: The crab holds up a <sound>to</sound>rch and sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
凸.kun: From a <sound>de</sound>ckchair beside it, a <sound>ko</sound>ala pats its own round tummy.

軒.meaning: An old <part>drying rack</part> is fed up with standing in the rain, so one night it climbs the wall and hooks itself under the edge of the roof. The socks still flap, but now they dry, and the family <part>car</part> parked below stays free of drips. The rack has found its favourite spot: the <kanji>eaves</kanji>.
軒.on: The dog's <sound>ken</sound>nel squeezes in under there too.
軒.kun: When the <sound>no</sound>rth wind blows, Dad hangs the car <sound>key</sound> on the rack with the socks.

甚.meaning: Two oxen share one <part>yoke</part> and pull an <part>equal</part> share of the plough, step for step. The farmer adds a sack, then a cart, then a cow, then his whole house. They pull it all without a grunt. They are <kanji>tremendously</kanji> strong.
甚.on: He rewards them with a bucket of <sound>gin</sound>ger roots.
甚.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the farmer, sharing his <sound>na</sound>an. '<sound>Ha</sound>!' the oxen snort back.

畑.meaning: A dragon retires to the countryside and buys a <part>rice field</part>, but she can't stop breathing <part>fire</part>. The water boils away, the paddies dry out and the frogs move next door. So she plants potatoes and carrots in the warm dry soil instead. Now it's a proper <kanji>farm</kanji>.
畑.kun: She plays her <sound>ha</sound>rp while a <sound>ta</sound>co warms on the <sound>ke</sound>ttle beside her potatoes.

沢.meaning: A surveyor comes to <part>measure</part> a field for a new car park. With every step his boots sink deeper, <part>water drops</part> seep up round his ankles, frogs sit on his notebook and a heron borrows his hat. He writes down the size anyway: one large <kanji>swamp</kanji>.
沢.on: At lunch the heron steals his <sound>taco</sound> as well.
沢.kun: He drops his <sound>sa</sound>rdine sandwich in the mud and cries, '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

耕.meaning: Every morning a farmer drags his <part>plough</part> in tight circles round the village <part>well</part>, because it's the only shady spot. Round and round, until the soil is soft as cake. By spring the well is ringed with sunflowers. It's the only place he likes to <kanji>till</kanji>.
耕.on: At noon he cools off with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
耕.kun: He plants a <sound>ta</sound>co shell, a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic and a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn to see what grows.

亜.meaning: A giant opens his <part>mouth</part> so wide it's propped by a tent <part>pole</part> on each side, with <part>one</part> lip above and one below. Inside, instead of teeth, there are deserts, jungles and snowy peaks. He has swallowed the biggest continent: <kanji>Asia</kanji>.
亜.on: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he says, like at the dentist, so you can see inside.
亜.kun: Then the dust makes him sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a little panda flies out.

欄.meaning: The village paper is pinned to a <part>tree</part> by the town <part>gate</part>. Each week the gossip writer rolls her news into a tight <part>bundle</part> and unrolls it down the trunk in one tall, thin strip. Readers walk round and round the tree. It's the most popular <kanji>column</kanji> in town.
欄.on: Pigeons glide in to read it, landing on the path as if it were a <sound>run</sound>way.
欄.kun: Below it, a <sound>te</sound>nt sells <sound>su</sound>shi to readers queuing along the <sound>ree</sound>d fence.
